candidates.text: System shall validate Tool Permissions before executing any Context Menu Tool and restrict unauthorized access.

candidates.text: If no Tool Permission is assigned to a User Group, no Context Menu Tools shall be visible or accessible to its users.
candidates.locator: § Tool Permission for Context Menu Actions

candidates.text:
Tool Permission for Context Menu Actions:
1. System shall provide a Tool Permission multi-select dropdown under Sales Order New Program Permissions to assign one or multiple Context Menu Tools to a User Group.
2. System shall display only the Grid Level and Header Level Context Menu Tools assigned to the logged-in user's User Group.
3. System shall validate Tool Permissions before executing any Context Menu Tool and restrict unauthorized access.
4. System shall support assigning multiple Tool Permissions to a User Group, allowing access to all selected Context Menu Tools.
5. If no Tool Permission is assigned to a User Group, no Context Menu Tools shall be visible or accessible to its users.
candidates.locator: § Tool Permission for Context Menu Actions

candidates.text:
Split Shuffle OC/DOC:
1. Disable and freeze the Target Delivery lookup.
2. Automatically create a new Draft Delivery upon clicking Load.
3. Copy all Delivery level information from the Source Delivery to the newly created Delivery.
4. Copy all selected Articles along with their Color/Size combinations, Selling Prices, Delivery details, Instructions, and all other applicable Delivery information.
5. Generate the new Delivery in Draft status.
6. Automatically open the newly created Delivery in editable mode after successful creation.

1. Enable the Target Delivery lookup.
2. Display only eligible Deliveries belonging to the same Sales Order for selection.
3. Allow the user to select one Target Delivery.
4. Transfer the split/shuffled quantities to the selected Target Delivery after confirmation.
5. No new Delivery shall be created in this scenario.
6. Recalculate the quantities and values for both the Source Delivery and Target Delivery.

candidates.text: The scope of this document is to define the functional requirement and system behaviour for Transfer Price Mapping and Transfer Price Order processing in WFX ERP, covering both Forward TP and Backward TP flows between the Order Company and Execution Company.
candidates.locator: § TP Mapping › Scope

candidates.text: This document is limited to functional mapping and process flow definition and does not cover detailed technical design, test scenarios, API details, accounting configuration, or open points.
candidates.locator: § TP Mapping › Scope

candidates.text: The purpose of this document is to formalize the required system behaviour for Transfer Price Order.
candidates.locator: § TP Mapping › Purpose

candidates.text: The key objective is to ensure that company-wise documents are created in the correct sequence and that auto-created documents remain linked between the Order Company and Execution Company.
candidates.locator: § TP Mapping › Purpose

candidates.text: The process is used when an order involves two related companies: one company owns the buyer order and another company executes production, procurement, shipment and internal billing.
candidates.locator: § TP Mapping › Overview

candidates.text: Before using Transfer Price Mapping, the user must first map the End Customer in Company Info.
candidates.locator: § TP Mapping › Solution › Company Info Mapping

candidates.text: In Order Company → Company Info, the user must map Buyer (End Customer) with the the Order Company.
candidates.locator: § TP Mapping › Solution › Company Info Mapping

candidates.text: In Order Company → Company Info, only the Buyer mapping is required as per this TP setup.
candidates.locator: § TP Mapping › Solution › Company Info Mapping

candidates.text: In Execution Company → Company Info, the user must map Supplier with the as the Execution Company supplier.
candidates.locator: § TP Mapping › Solution › Company Info Mapping

candidates.text: This Company Info setup is mandatory before creating or using TP Mapping.

chunks.title: Tool Permission for Context Menu Actions
chunks.heading: Tool Permission for Context Menu Actions
chunks.text:
Navigation:
Admin → Organisation Structure → User Master → User Groups → Program Permissions → Sales Order New → Tool Permission
A new permission section named Tool Permission shall be available under Sales Order New Program Permissions.
Administrators can assign tool access permissions to User Groups through a multi-select dropdown. Based on the selected permissions, the system shall control the visibility and execution of Context Menu Tools available in the Sales Order New screen.
Validations:
• System shall provide a Tool Permission multi-select dropdown under Sales Order New Program Permissions to assign one or multiple Context Menu Tools to a User Group.
• System shall display only the Grid Level and Header Level Context Menu Tools assigned to the logged-in user's User Group.
• System shall validate Tool Permissions before executing any Context Menu Tool and restrict unauthorized access.
• System shall support assigning multiple Tool Permissions to a User Group, allowing access to all selected Context Menu Tools.
• If no Tool Permission is assigned to a User Group, no Context Menu Tools shall be visible or accessible to its users.
chunks.locator: § Tool Permission for Context Menu Actions

chunks.title: Split Shuffle OC/DOC
chunks.heading: Sales Order List (New Addition) › Grid Level Context Menu › Split Shuffle OC/DOC
chunks.text:
Navigation: Sales Order List -> Grid Level Context Menu -> Split Shuffle OC/DOC
Split / Shuffle OC/DOC:
The Split / Shuffle OC/DOC functionality shall enable the user to distribute the quantities of an existing Delivery either by creating a New Delivery or by transferring the quantities to an Existing Delivery belonging to the same Sales Order.
Upon clicking the Split/Shuffle action against a Delivery, the system shall open the Split / Shuffle popup. The popup shall contain the following fields:
• Source Delivery (Display Only)
• Target Delivery OC
• Target Deliveries
• From Delivery OC
• From Deliveries
• Confirm
• Discard
• Edit
• Load
Target Delivery OC
The Target Delivery OC field shall contain the following values:
• New Delivery
• Existing Delivery
The behaviour of the screen shall change dynamically based on the selected value.
• Target Delivery OC = New Delivery (Fully Editable)
When the user selects New Delivery, the system shall:
• Disable and freeze the Target Delivery lookup.
• Automatically create a new Draft Delivery upon clicking Load.
• Copy all Delivery level information from the Source Delivery to the newly created Delivery.
• Copy all selected Articles along with their Color/Size combinations, Selling Prices, Delivery details, Instructions, and all other applicable Delivery information.
• Generate the new Delivery in Draft status.
chunks.locator: § Sales Order List (New Addition) › Grid Level Context Menu › Split Shuffle OC/DOC

chunks.title: Split Shuffle OC/DOC
chunks.heading: Sales Order List (New Addition) › Grid Level Context Menu › Split Shuffle OC/DOC
chunks.text:
• Automatically open the newly created Delivery in editable mode after successful creation.
• Keep the Buyer Order Reference blank. This field shall not be copied from the Source Delivery and must be entered manually by the user before saving or confirming the Delivery.
• Target Delivery OC = Existing Delivery (Delivery is not editable Only Split functionality Works)
When the user selects Existing Delivery, the system shall:
• Enable the Target Delivery lookup.
• Display only eligible Deliveries belonging to the same Sales Order for selection.
• Allow the user to select one Target Delivery.
• Transfer the split/shuffled quantities to the selected Target Delivery after confirmation.
• No new Delivery shall be created in this scenario.
• Recalculate the quantities and values for both the Source Delivery and Target Delivery.
Target Delivery Eligibility
The Target Delivery lookup shall display only those Deliveries that satisfy all of the following conditions:
• Belong to the same Sales Order.
• Belong to the same Buyer.
• Belong to the same Style/OC.
• Are in Draft or Editable status.
• Are not Cancelled.
• Are not Closed.
• User has modification permission for the Delivery.
The Source Delivery shall not be available for selection as the Target Delivery.
Split Mode
The Split Mode shall contain two options:
• Quantity
• Percentage
Only one mode can be selected at a time.
chunks.locator: § Sales Order List (New Addition) › Grid Level Context Menu › Split Shuffle OC/DOC (part 2)

chunks.title: Split Shuffle OC/DOC
chunks.heading: Sales Order List (New Addition) › Grid Level Context Menu › Split Shuffle OC/DOC
chunks.text:
Split by Quantity
When Quantity mode is selected:
• The user shall enter the quantity to be transferred.
• The entered quantity shall be distributed proportionately across all selected Article Color/Size combinations.
• The transferred quantity shall be deducted from the Source Delivery.
• The Target Delivery shall receive the calculated quantities.
• All Delivery totals shall be recalculated automatically.
Split by Percentage
When Percentage mode is selected:
• The user shall enter the split percentage.
• The system shall calculate the quantity for each Article Color/Size combination using:
Split Quantity = Existing Quantity × Split Percentage / 100
• Quantities shall be rounded according to the configured UOM precision.
• The calculated quantity shall be transferred to the Target Delivery.
• Remaining quantity shall stay in the Source Delivery.
• Delivery totals shall be recalculated automatically.
Data to be Copied
The following information shall be copied during Split/Shuffling:
• Buyer
• Buyer Division
• Category
• Season
• Delivery Dates
• Factory
• Currency
• Destination
• Country
• Shipping Details
• Packing Details
• Purchase Officer
• Delivery Terms
• Articles
• Selling Prices
• Selected Colors
• Selected Sizes
• Instructions
• Documents (if applicable)
• Other Delivery level information
The following information shall not be copied:
• Buyer Order Reference
chunks.locator: § Sales Order List (New Addition) › Grid Level Context Menu › Split Shuffle OC/DOC (part 3)

chunks.title: Split Shuffle OC/DOC
chunks.heading: Sales Order List (New Addition) › Grid Level Context Menu › Split Shuffle OC/DOC
chunks.text:
• Delivery Number
• Approval Details
• Workflow Status
• Audit Information
Quantity Distribution
For every selected Article, the system shall automatically:
• Calculate Color-wise quantity.
• Calculate Size-wise quantity.
• Calculate Article Total Quantity.
• Calculate Article Value.
• Calculate Delivery Total Quantity.
• Calculate Delivery Total Value.
All calculations shall immediately update both Source and Target Deliveries.
Validations
The system shall validate the following before processing Split/Shuffle:
General Validations
• Split Mode is mandatory.
• Split Value is mandatory.
• At least one Article must exist.
• At least one Color/Size combination must exist.
• Source Delivery must be editable.
• Delivery Status shall not be Cancelled or Closed.
Target Delivery Validations
For New Delivery
• Target Delivery lookup shall remain disabled.
• No Target Delivery selection shall be permitted.
For Existing Delivery
• Target Delivery selection is mandatory.
• Source Delivery and Target Delivery cannot be the same.
• Target Delivery must belong to the same Sales Order.
• Target Delivery must belong to the same Buyer.
• Target Delivery must be editable.
• Target Delivery shall not be Cancelled or Closed.
Quantity Validations
When Split Mode is Quantity:
• Quantity must be greater than zero.
• Quantity cannot exceed available Delivery quantity.
• Quantity cannot be negative.
chunks.locator: § Sales Order List (New Addition) › Grid Level Context Menu › Split Shuffle OC/DOC (part 4)

chunks.title: Split Shuffle OC/DOC
chunks.heading: Sales Order List (New Addition) › Grid Level Context Menu › Split Shuffle OC/DOC
chunks.text:
Percentage Validations
When Split Mode is Percentage:
• Percentage must be greater than 0.
• Percentage cannot exceed 100.
• Decimal values shall be accepted as per configured precision.
Buyer Order Reference Validation
For every newly created Delivery:
• Buyer Order Reference shall remain blank.
• User shall be required to enter Buyer Order Reference before Save or Confirm.
• System shall not allow Save/Confirm until Buyer Order Reference is entered.
System Audit
The following actions shall be captured in the History/Audit Trail:
• Split Created
• Shuffle Completed
• Source Delivery
• Target Delivery
• Split Mode
• Split Quantity/Percentage
• User Name
• Date & Time
• Remarks (if entered)
Success Messages
• "Delivery has been successfully split into a new Draft Delivery."
• "Selected quantities have been successfully transferred to the Target Delivery."
Error Messages
• Please select Target Delivery.
• Source and Target Delivery cannot be the same.
• Target Delivery is not editable.
• Split Quantity cannot exceed available quantity.
• Split Percentage must be between 0 and 100.
• Buyer Order Reference is mandatory.
• No Article exists for Split/Shuffle.
• Color/Size selection is mandatory.
• Delivery cannot be processed in its current status.
chunks.locator: § Sales Order List (New Addition) › Grid Level Context Menu › Split Shuffle OC/DOC (part 5)

chunks.title: Delivery OC Notes
chunks.heading: Sales Order List (New Addition) › Grid Level Context Menu › Notes › Delivery OC Notes
chunks.text:
Within a Delivery OC, the user shall be able to add Notes through the Notes action.
Notes Popup
When the user clicks Notes, the system shall open the Notes popup.
The popup shall contain:
• Notes (Mandatory Dropdown)
• Save
• Cancel
The Notes dropdown shall display only Active OC Notes configured from:
Sales → Codes → OC Notes
The dropdown shall be searchable.
Save
When the user selects a Note and clicks Save:
The system shall:
• Associate the selected Note with the current Delivery OC.
• Record the User Name.
• Record Date & Time.
• Add a new entry in the Activity Timeline of the Delivery.
• Close the popup.
• Display a success message.
The Activity Timeline entry shall include:
• Note Description
• User Name
• Date & Time
• Activity Type = "OC Note Added"
A Delivery may have multiple Notes added over time.
Each Save action shall create a separate Activity Timeline entry.
Cancel
When the user clicks Cancel:
• The popup shall close.
• No Note shall be associated with the Delivery.
• No Activity Timeline entry shall be created.
chunks.locator: § Sales Order List (New Addition) › Grid Level Context Menu › Notes › Delivery OC Notes

chunks.title: OC Notes Master Configuration
chunks.heading: Sales Order List (New Addition) › Grid Level Context Menu › Notes › OC Notes Master Configuration
chunks.text:
Navigation
Sales → Codes → OC Notes
The OC Notes master shall allow users to maintain the list of standard Notes available throughout the Sales module.
Screen Behaviour
The screen shall display the following columns:
• OC Notes
• Active
The following actions shall be available from the toolbar:
• Add
• Save
• Delete
• Discard/Cancel
Add Note
When the user clicks Add:
• A new editable row shall be added to the grid.
• The user shall enter the OC Note.
• Active shall be checked by default.
• The Note field shall be mandatory.
Save Note
When the user clicks Save:
The system shall validate:
• OC Note is entered.
• Duplicate Notes are not allowed.
Upon successful validation:
• The Note shall be saved.
• The Note shall become available for selection in every Delivery OC Notes popup.
• Success message shall be displayed.
Delete Note
When the user clicks Delete:
• Selected Note(s) shall be deleted.
• Deleted Notes shall no longer appear in the Delivery Notes dropdown.
• If a deleted Note is already associated with an existing Delivery, it shall remain visible in the Activity Timeline for audit purposes but shall not be available for future selection.
Discard
When the user clicks Discard:
• All unsaved changes shall be reverted.
• No data shall be saved.
chunks.locator: § Sales Order List (New Addition) › Grid Level Context Menu › Notes › OC Notes Master Configuration

chunks.title: Cancel Delivery OC
chunks.heading: Sales Order List (New Addition) › Grid Level Context Menu › Cancel Delivery OC
chunks.text:
Navigation
Sales → Sales Order List → Grid Level Context Menu → Cancel Delivery OC
Process Flow
• The user selects one or more Delivery OC(s) from the Sales Order List.
• The user clicks Cancel Delivery OC from the Grid Level Context Menu.
• The system displays a Cancel Delivery OC confirmation pop-up.
• Upon clicking Continue, the system opens the Remarks Add-on page for the selected Delivery OC(s), allowing the user to enter cancellation remarks.
• After entering the remarks, the user clicks OK.
• The system displays a Confirm Order Cancellation dialog with the following message:
Are you sure you want to cancel the selected Delivery OC?
Cancelling the selected Delivery OC will also cancel all corresponding:
• Delivery OC(s)
• Production Order(s)
• FPO(s)
This action cannot be undone.
• The user clicks Confirm Cancellation.
• The system performs the following actions:
• Cancels the selected Delivery OC(s).
• Cancels all associated Production Order(s).
• Cancels all associated FPO(s).
• Updates the status of the Delivery OC(s) to Cancelled.
• Saves the cancellation remarks in the system for audit and tracking purposes.
chunks.locator: § Sales Order List (New Addition) › Grid Level Context Menu › Cancel Delivery OC

chunks.title: Cancel
chunks.heading: Sales Order List (New Addition) › Grid Level Context Menu › Cancel
chunks.text:
Navigation
Sales → Sales Order List → Grid Level Context Menu → Cancel
Process Flow
• When the user selects Cancel from the Grid Level Context Menu, the system shall display a Cancel Order confirmation pop-up.
Message:
Please note that this action will cancel all Delivery OC(s) associated with this Main OC. Do you want to continue?
• If the user clicks Continue, the system shall open the Cancellation Remarks pop-up.
• The user shall enter the Remarks / Reason (Mandatory) and click OK.
• Upon clicking OK, the system shall:
• Cancel the selected Main Order (OC).
• Cancel all associated Delivery OC(s).
• Save the cancellation remarks.
• Update the Order Status to Cancelled.
• If the user clicks Cancel on either pop-up, the cancellation process shall be aborted, and no changes shall be made.
Validation
If the user attempts to cancel an Order whose status is Saved, Cancelled, or Closed, the system shall not initiate the cancellation process.
Instead, the system shall display the following information message:
Title: Order Cancellation Not Allowed
Message:
You cannot cancel a Saved, Cancelled, or Closed Order.
Clicking OK shall close the dialog, and the Order Gets closed and status gets updated.
chunks.locator: § Sales Order List (New Addition) › Grid Level Context Menu › Cancel

chunks.title: Close
chunks.heading: Sales Order List (New Addition) › Grid Level Context Menu › Close
chunks.text:
Navigation
Sales → Sales Order List → Grid Level Context Menu → Close
Process Flow
• When the user selects Close from the Grid Level Context Menu, the system shall display the Close Order pop-up.
• The pop-up shall display a Remarks / Reason field, which is mandatory for closing the Order.
• The user shall enter the closing remarks and click Close Order.
• Upon clicking Close Order, the system shall:
• Validate that the Remarks / Reason field is populated.
• Close the selected Order (OC).
• Update the Order Status to Closed.
• Save the closing remarks for audit and tracking purposes.
• Display a success message confirming that the Order has been closed successfully.
• If the user clicks Cancel or closes the pop-up, the closing process shall be aborted, and no changes shall be made.
Validation
If the user attempts to close an Order whose status is already Closed or Cancelled, the system shall not proceed with the close operation.
The system shall display the following information message:
Title: Order Closure Not Allowed
Message:
You cannot close a Cancelled or Closed Order.
Clicking OK shall close the dialog, and no changes shall be made to the Order.
chunks.locator: § Sales Order List (New Addition) › Grid Level Context Menu › Close

chunks.title: Inseam
chunks.heading: Inseam
chunks.text:
Inseam is a size categorization used to differentiate garments based on the inside leg length. It allows the same waist or garment size to be offered in multiple length variants to meet the sizing standards of different regions, countries, or customer groups.
Examples of Inseam categories include:
• Petite
• Missy
• Regular
• Tall
• Long
• Short
Configuration
• All Inseam values are maintained in the Size Master.
• Each Size Master record can be associated with an Inseam category.
• The Inseam values configured in the Size Master become available throughout the system wherever Inseam-based size classification is required.
Usage
The configured Inseam values are displayed in the Inseam dropdown available within the Color/Size Selection pop-up.
When creating or editing Color/Size combinations:
• The user selects the appropriate Inseam value for each size.
• This selection classifies the size under the corresponding Inseam group.
• Multiple sizes can belong to the same Inseam category.
• The selected Inseam value is stored against the respective Color/Size combination.
chunks.locator: § Inseam

chunks.title: Scope
chunks.heading: TP Mapping › Scope
chunks.text: The scope of this document is to define the functional requirement and system behaviour for Transfer Price Mapping and Transfer Price Order processing in WFX ERP, covering both Forward TP and Backward TP flows between the Order Company and Execution Company. It includes Company Info Mapping, TP Mapping setup, buyer/end customer/supplier/division mapping, price applicability, document auto-creation, and the complete transaction sequence across both companies, including OC, Techpack, Costing, GMPO, BOM, MRL, production, ASN, invoices, clearing and posting. This document is limited to functional mapping and process flow definition and does not cover detailed technical design, test scenarios, API details, accounting configuration, or open points.
chunks.locator: § TP Mapping › Scope

chunks.title: Purpose
chunks.heading: TP Mapping › Purpose
chunks.text:
The purpose of this document is to formalize the required system behaviour for Transfer Price Order. The document explains the required mapping, assumptions, and functional solution for Forward TP and Backward TP without including detailed test scenarios or open-point sections.
The key objective is to ensure that company-wise documents are created in the correct sequence and that auto-created documents remain linked between the Order Company and Execution Company.
chunks.locator: § TP Mapping › Purpose

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.heading: TP Mapping › Overview
chunks.text:
This document defines the requirement for the Transfer Price Order process in WFX ERP. The process is used when an order involves two related companies: one company owns the buyer order and another company executes production, procurement, shipment and internal billing.
The requirement covers both Forward TP and Backward TP flows. In Forward TP, the order starts in the Order Company and the required execution documents are auto-created in the Execution Company. In Backward TP, the order starts in the Execution Company and the linked order is auto-created in the Parent / Order Company.
As per the Forward TP production cycle, the Order Company starts with Techpack, OC, Costing and GMPO. After that, Techpack, OC and Costing are created in the Execution Company, followed by BOM, MRL, procurement, production, Sales ASN and auto document generation back in the Order Company.
chunks.locator: § TP Mapping › Overview

chunks.title: Company Info Mapping
chunks.heading: TP Mapping › Solution › Company Info Mapping
chunks.text:
Before using Transfer Price Mapping, the user must first map the End Customer in Company Info.
In Order Company → Company Info, the user must map Buyer (End Customer) with the the Order Company.
In Order Company → Company Info, only the Buyer mapping is required as per this TP setup.
In Execution Company → Company Info, the user must map Supplier with the as the Execution Company supplier.
This Company Info setup is mandatory before creating or using TP Mapping.
TP Mapping shall use the Company Info setup to identify the correct internal buyer/supplier relationship between Order Company and Execution Company.
Path: Admin Company Info

chunks.title: Backward Transfer Price
chunks.heading: TP Mapping › Solution › Transfer Price Mapping › Backward Transfer Price
chunks.text:
There are four ways to apply price applicable on
• Default Margin % on FOB,
• Default Margin % on Material Cost in Internal Costsheet,
• Default Margin Rate,
• Default Selling Price.
chunks.locator: § TP Mapping › Solution › Transfer Price Mapping › Backward Transfer Price

chunks.title: Forward Transfer Price
chunks.heading: TP Mapping › Solution › Transfer Price Mapping › Forward Transfer Price
chunks.text: In Forward TP, the mapping is created in Default Transfer Price Mapping by selecting the Forward TP radio button. This mapping decides how the system will auto-create Techpack / Costsheet / OC in Execution Company when the source transaction is created from Order Company.
chunks.locator: § TP Mapping › Solution › Transfer Price Mapping › Forward Transfer Price

chunks.title: Backward Transfer Price
chunks.heading: TP Mapping › Solution › Transfer Price – Flow › Backward Transfer Price
chunks.text:
In Backward TP, the order starts in the Execution Company.
The process is:
• User creates OC in Execution Company.
• User selects Buyer.
• User selects Buyer Department.
• User selects End Customer.
• Execution Company Selling Price is auto-populated from Execution Company Default Selling Price.
• System auto-creates GMPO / OC in Order Company with .Auto suffix.
• Execution Company completes RM procurement.
• Execution Company completes production.
• User creates Sales ASN in Execution Company.
• User enters proper Execution Company and ETD / ETA Date in Sales ASN Shipping Info.
• System auto-creates GMPO GRN in Order Company.
• System auto-creates Supplier Invoice in Order Company.
• System auto-creates OC Sales ASN in Order Company.
• User manually creates Consignment Sales Invoice in Order Company.
• User manually performs clearing and posting in Order Company.
• System auto-creates Sales Invoice in Execution Company.
chunks.locator: § TP Mapping › Solution › Transfer Price – Flow › Backward Transfer Price

chunks.title: Forward Transfer Price
chunks.heading: TP Mapping › Solution › Transfer Price – Flow › Forward Transfer Price
chunks.text:
In Forward TP, the order starts in the Order Company.
The process is:
• User creates Techpack in Order Company.
• User creates OC in Order Company.
• User creates and approves costing in Order Company.
• User creates GMPO in Order Company.
• System auto-creates Techpack in Execution Company.
• System auto-creates OC in Execution Company.
• System auto-creates costing in open mode in Execution Company.
• User adds local purchase articles in Execution Company costing.
• User approves costing in Execution Company.
• User creates BOM manually in Execution Company.
• System generates MRL after BOM and OC creation.
• System generates production after MRL.
• User creates FPO manually.
• System creates FPPO based on Auto PD selected in BOM.
• User performs output against FPPO.
• System / user performs SF / FG QC.
• User creates Sales ASN manually in Execution Company.
• FG is dispatched from Execution Company.
• System auto-creates Sourcing ASN in Order Company.
• System auto-creates Inter Purchase Invoice in Order Company.
• System auto-creates Sales ASN in Order Company.
chunks.locator: § TP Mapping › Solution › Transfer Price – Flow › Forward Transfer Price
